# omni_cluster_wait (Resource)

Waits for an Omni cluster to become ready: every machine set running and ready, every requested machine allocated and healthy, the control plane ready, the Kubernetes API reachable, and the cluster running the Talos and Kubernetes versions it is configured with, so that a wait after an upgrade only ends once the upgrade is done. It is what the Omni UI shows as a cluster that is up.

Omni brings a cluster up asynchronously, so `omni_cluster` and `omni_machine_set_node` are done as soon as Omni has accepted them. Depend on this resource from anything that needs the cluster working, such as a Kubernetes provider pointed at it, and make it depend on the machine set nodes so it starts waiting once they all exist.

Only creating this resource waits. Refreshing it reads the cluster status once and never blocks a plan. Changing `machine_ids` waits again; to wait again after any other change, the cluster upgraded for instance, put something that changes with it in `triggers`. Destroying it does nothing to the cluster.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "omni_cluster" "example" {
  name               = "example"
  talos_version      = "1.14.5"
  kubernetes_version = "1.37.1"
}

resource "omni_machine_set" "control_plane" {
  cluster = omni_cluster.example.name
  role    = "controlplane"
}

resource "omni_machine_set_node" "control_plane" {
  for_each = toset(var.control_plane_machine_ids)

  cluster     = omni_cluster.example.name
  machine_set = omni_machine_set.control_plane.id
  machine_id  = each.value
}

# Omni brings the cluster up after Terraform has created the resources above. This waits until it
# is up: machine sets running, every machine healthy, control plane and Kubernetes API ready.
resource "omni_cluster_wait" "example" {
  cluster = omni_cluster.example.name

  # The machines the cluster should end up with. Referencing the nodes also makes this wait start
  # once they all exist, and a changed set of machines waits again, including for removed machines
  # to be taken out.
  machine_ids = [for node in omni_machine_set_node.control_plane : node.machine_id]

  # Wait again after an upgrade, too.
  triggers = {
    talos_version      = omni_cluster.example.talos_version
    kubernetes_version = omni_cluster.example.kubernetes_version
  }

  timeouts = {
    create = "45m"
  }
}

# Anything that needs a working cluster depends on the wait.
output "cluster_ready" {
  value = omni_cluster_wait.example.ready
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster` (String) The name of the cluster to wait for.

### Optional

- `machine_ids` (Set of String) The UUIDs of the machines the cluster should have. When set, the cluster is only ready once its machines are exactly these, each of them running and ready, and changing them waits again. Set it whenever machines are removed: Terraform may start waiting before Omni has begun taking the removed machines out, and the cluster still reports ready with them in it, so without this the wait could end before the scale down has even started.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))
- `triggers` (Map of String) Arbitrary values that, when changed, make Terraform wait for the cluster again, for instance its Talos and Kubernetes versions.

### Read-Only

- `machines_healthy` (Number) How many of the cluster's machines are healthy.
- `machines_total` (Number) How many machines the cluster has.
- `phase` (String) The cluster phase Omni reports, such as `Running` or `ScalingUp`.
- `ready` (Boolean) Whether the cluster is ready. Always true right after the wait; a later refresh reports what Omni says at that time.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the cluster, as a Go duration. Defaults to 30m0s.
